claims.text: Pulumi programs can reference existing Terraform state files (e.g., to read outputs from Terraform-managed infrastructure).
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly from Pulumi.
HCL code can be converted to Pulumi code.
Terraform and Pulumi deployments can be orchestrated together.

The `@pulumi/terraform` package exposes a class `terraform.state.S3Reference` that takes `bucket` and `key` arguments and exposes a `getOutput(name)` method for reading outputs from a Terraform state file stored in S3.
The automation module import (`import * as pulumi from "@pulumi/pulumi/automation"`) exposes `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`, usable to reference a Terraform state in S3 with `bucket` and `key`.

`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")` retrieves an output named vpcId from another Pulumi stack; the example comments that the core infrastructure stack 'could be Terraform'.
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` (value `"DEFAULT"`) properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
Terraform state ownership can be transferred to Pulumi gradually, resource-by-resource (state migration).

`pulumi import` takes a resource type token, a resource name, and a cloud resource ID, e.g. `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, and `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster` are valid AWS type tokens.

A Pulumi import API exists that can be used programmatically within a program to import resources (the migration helper comments 'Use Pulumi import API to import resources'), and `getOutput("resources")` on a Terraform state reference returns an awaitable list of state resources.
Pulumi policies (Policy Packs) can enforce infrastructure policies across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.

The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`; policies take `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel: "mandatory"`, and `validateResource` whose callback signature is `(resource, args, reportViolation)`.
`aws.ec2.Instance` resource inputs expose a `tags` property and `aws.s3.Bucket` exposes an `acl` property that can be `"public-read"` or `"public-read-write"`.
The Pulumi Automation API allows embedding Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Automation API (`@pulumi/pulumi/automation`) provides `LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({stackName, projectName, program})`, `stack.setConfig(key, {value})`, and `stack.up({onOutput})` returning a result with `outputs`.
Component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving the complexity of multi-tool management to the platform team rather than development teams.
`@pulumi/terraform` is a Pulumi package importable as `terraform` in TypeScript programs.
`pulumi.ComponentResource` takes a type token, name, args, and options via `super("custom:WebApplication", name, {}, opts)` and supports `registerOutputs`.
Developers can create WebApplication component resources in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources.
The page /docs/intro/concepts/ exists and is a deep dive into Pulumi's architecture.
The page /docs/using-pulumi/adopting-pulumi/ exists and provides comprehensive migration strategies.
The page /docs/intro/vs/terraform/ exists and provides a detailed comparison of Pulumi and Terraform features.
The page /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/ exists and covers programmatic infrastructure management.
The page /docs/insights/policy/ exists and covers Policy as Code for infrastructure governance and compliance.
The Pulumi Community page at pulumi.com/community/ lets you join the community Slack and forum.
The github.com/pulumi/examples repository contains hundreds of real-world examples.
The Pulumi Blog provides the latest updates and case studies.
The Pulumi YouTube channel at youtube.com/pulumitv exists and hosts video tutorials and demos.
Pulumi's Snowflake case study (pulumi.com/case-studies/snowflake/) exists and describes how Snowflake uses Pulumi with existing tools, framed as a multi-cloud strategy.
Pulumi's Mercedes-Benz case study (pulumi.com/case-studies/mercedes-benz/) exists and describes large-scale infrastructure modernization via platform engineering.
Pulumi's Lemonade case study (pulumi.com/case-studies/lemonade/) exists and describes rapid development by Lemonade using Pulumi and Terraform.
The Pulumi Community Slack is at slack.pulumi.com and provides real-time community support.
The github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues tracker is the place for Pulumi bug reports and feature requests.
support.pulumi.com provides professional support for Pulumi Cloud customers.
The pulumi/pulumi repository has a CONTRIBUTING.md on the `master` branch (github.com/pulumi/pulumi/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md).
The page /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/ exists and covers creating new providers and components.
The pulumi/examples repository has a CONTRIBUTING.md on the `master` branch (github.com/pulumi/examples/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) for sharing patterns.
pulumi.com/blog/, pulumi.com/events/, and pulumi.com/community/ exist, supporting writing about experiences, speaking at meetups/conferences, and joining or starting local user groups.
Feedback can be given via the Pulumi Community Slack or by opening an issue at github.com/pulumi/docs/issues.
